newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Nationalists uproot HK stake to Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Nationalists uproot HK stake to Singapore.

text.p: Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party, one of the world's richest parties, has moved its Hong Kong holding company to Singapore to prevent it becoming subject to communist China's control, local media said on Tuesday.

The move aims to protect Hong Kong assets worth hundreds of millions of U.S. dollars after Britain hands the colony back to Beijing on July 1, the Economic Daily News quoted senior Nationalist officials as saying.

The Nationalist Party, whose seven holding companies handle investments in 121 Taiwan companies, had total assets of over T$85 billion (US$3.09 billion) as of the end of December, Taiwan media have reported.
The Economic Daily said the party's Hong Kong holding company owned a trading firm and several unspecified properties.
Party officials in Taipei could not be reached for comment.
Hong Kong is the main conduit through which more than US$20 billion in Taiwan investment has flowed into the mainland.
The Nationalists, with 2.6 million members, have ruled Taiwan since their Republic of China government lost a civil war to the communists in 1949 and fled into exile on the island.

The party's once-unshaken power has weakened since tbe legalisation of opposition political parties in the late 1980s started Taiwan's democratic renaissance, and Beijing suspects Taiwan is plotting to become an independent country.
Taipei espouses eventual unification with the mainland but only after China adopts multiparty reforms like Taiwan's own.
Taiwan has flatly rejected the "one country, two systems" model of local autonomy that Beijing has put forth as the key to Taiwan's reunification and will implement in Hong Kong.
Beijing has promised to leave Hong Kong's capitalist system and way of life intact for 50 years after the handover, but the Nationalist government on Taiwan remains deeply suspicious.
"We cannot accept...the 'one country, two systems' proposal. It is impossible," President Lee Teng-hui told German television in a recent interview recounted by his office.

"When (mainland paramount leader) Deng Xiaoping proposed 'one country, two systems', what is this one country which is referred to? Does it mean the (communist) People's Republic of China or the (Nationalist) Republic of China? It is not clear.
"Under these circumstances, making such a proposal is unreasonable," Lee said.
Beijing froze what had been slowly warming talks in June 1995 and mounted nine months of war games and missile tests in the Taiwan Strait after Lee made a private visit to the United States.
Beijing cited the visit as evidence that Lee secretly wanted a sovereign, independent Taiwan despite his government's public advocacy of eventual unification.
